scope.summary: Author the height and global frame channels per Section 13.17 (BK-17.3, TAI-BK-051), closing REQ-005: height decomposed into limb/torso ratio channels (leg_length, torso_length, arm_length, overall_scale) rather than a single uniform scale, so 'petite' is a designed axis set usable simultaneously with ANY tissue channel at maximum. Petite + max breasts + narrow shoulders + small hands must render artifact-free.
acceptance_criteria: arm_length and overall_scale registered kind Skeletal (leg_length and torso_length already exist from MT-503/504; this MT wires the four into a coherent 'frame' group with a derived read-only height_cm measurement).

height_cm is a derived measurement (from evaluated skeleton), not a writable channel; GET returns it in cm and PUT on it is rejected with a pointer to the ratio channels (single-uniform-scale prohibition).

Petite acceptance sample (REQ-005): overall_scale at petite minimum + leg_length low + breast_volume 3.0 + shoulder_frame_width min + hand_scale min evaluates artifact-free with mesh-quality and joint-derivation assertions — the archetype (a) frame proof.
Each frame channel sweep passes BODY_DECOUPLE_VALID (skeletal writes only within declared skeletal semantics; zero tissue-mask delta writes).
overall_scale composes multiplicatively with per-segment lengths without double-scaling (a 2.0 overall + 1.5 leg_length test asserts expected femur length).
scope.risk_if_missed: A single height dial is how existing tools couple frame to everything else; without decomposed ratio axes, 'petite with unrealistically large tits' — the operator's founding production body — cannot be dialed without fighting proportions.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > BodyKit shape channels and measurements

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT emits typed diagnostics through its owning command or job and inherits retention, health, and projection behavior from the shared diagnostics substrate.
The owning native shell or scheduled job supplies Palmistry coverage; this MT must preserve operation identity and recovery handles.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

required_changes_before_execution: Separate control independence from declared feathered deformation support, skeletal propagation, physical response, and explicit coupling.
Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.
